note: Five warships with measured trial power and speed. Lengths are between perpendiculars, values are SI, and each case records the load condition it was taken at: mixing conditions moved Hood's error by thirteen points, so the condition is part of the datum.
units: SI in the file (m, t, shp, kn); the kernel converts once at the boundary

cases.name: HMS Dreadnought (1906)
cases.source: RN trials 9 Oct 1906: 21.6 kn from 27,018 shp (Wikipedia prose, trial sentence); LBP 490 ft, LOA 527 ft
cases.condition_note: displacement 18,411 t is the as-built normal load; the draught 9.03 m is nearer deep load than the 26.5 ft (8.08 m) normal figure

cases.name: HMS Hood (1920)
cases.source: 1920 full power trial, 42,200 t: 151,280 shp at 32.07 kn (Wikipedia prose, trial sentence)
cases.condition_note: trial displacement 42,200 t as stated in the trial record; the draught 9.75 m is the deep-load figure, so the block coefficient carries that mixture

cases.name: HMS Repulse (1916)
cases.source: 1916 trials: 118,913 shp at 31.73 kn (Wikipedia prose, trial sentence)

cases.name: HMS Renown (1916)
cases.source: 1916 trials: 126,000 shp at 32.58 kn (Wikipedia prose, trial sentence)

cases.name: Bismarck (1940)
cases.source: kbismarck.com testing record: the plant designed for 138,000 hp and 29 kn 'actually obtained 150,170 hp and 30.1 knots'
